articles.headline: Six tries and a big win - but were Ireland ruthless?
keyFacts: Ireland defeated Argentina 42-12 with six tries in Dublin, though head coach Andy Farrell stated his team missed a chance to be ruthless.
Captain Dan Sheehan, Robert Baloucoune, Sean Jansen, Josh van der Flier, and Mack Hansen all sustained injuries during the match.
Ireland will play Fiji in Dublin on 14 November before facing South Africa later in the international window.
body: - Published
Before Ireland's Nations Championship game with Argentina, head coach Andy Farrell had been honest about where his side are less than a year out from the World Cup.

He admitted his team must improve if they are to challenge in Australia next year - a stark contrast to four years ago when they were riding the crest of a wave before they fell short in the quarter-finals.
Despite Mateo Carreras' early try, Ireland had far too much for Los Pumas in Dublin as they ran out 42-12 winners under the Friday night lights.
Hugo Keenan stole the headlines with his hat-trick, while Dan Sheehan, Sam Prendergast and Ronan Kelleher also crossed.
But despite scoring six tries and winning by a 30-point margin, Farrell was left wanting more.
Ireland had 59% territory throughout the game, and also edged possession, but did not score after the 55th minute when Kelleher rounded off a rolling maul.
"The scoreline is a good one because not many teams do that to Argentina, they are a dangerous side," Farrell said.
"I thought there was outstanding stuff and some clinical stuff, but I think the story of the game is we missed a chance to be ruthless.
"Having said that, the opportunities we had in the right end of the field showed the dominance in field position and territory."
One concern for Farrell will be an injury list - and a lengthy one at that.
Captain Dan Sheehan was forced off in the first half after he failed a head injury assessment, although Farrell said he "seems fine in the dressing room".
Wing Robert Baloucoune was forced off with a knock, while Sean Jansen sustained a "bang" to his knee and Josh van der Flier and Mack Hansen both have ankle concerns.
The injuries to Baloucoune, who went off in the 58th minute, and Hansen, who continued after receiving treatment, will be particularly concerning after the performance of Farrell's back three.

They had only played once together before, four years ago against South Africa, and Keenan's first try of the evening came off the back of a flowing move, when Baloucoune powered into space and found Hansen, who in turn set up the full-back to score.
That was the catalyst for Ireland's turnaround - and a hat-trick for Keenan in his first home match since the 2025 Six Nations came a year since Hansen's treble against Australia in Dublin.
All of Farrell's back three trio have struggled with injuries in the past year, and Friday's win was a glimpse of Ireland's attacking potential if they can stay fit and in form.
"I thought back three outstanding. Hugo Keenan, 22 months since he played here and didn't remember what side of the pitch we warmed up, which was a bit of an insult.
"He was immense. Same with Mack and Rob. They pace they put onto the ball and they were a threat. I'm delighted with the back three."
Ireland 'weathered the storm'
Beirne said that Argentina "came out firing" in Dublin as they chased a first away win over Ireland, something that came as no surprise to the Irish pack.
"We weathered the storm and got into how we wanted to play the game," said Beirne.
"What was pleasing about that was some of those tries were proper team tries and everyone was involved with them. That was the biggest takeaway from the game that."
But, like Farrell, the second row believes there is more to come at the attacking end of the pitch.
"We probably came away a little bit frustrated because we felt we didn't capitalise on a lot of the territory at the end of the game and the chances we had.
"That shows how good a performance it was to come away feeling like that."
After a bruising opener, Farrell will be forced to assess his squad ahead of Fiji's visit to Dublin on 14 November.
After that, world champions South Africa will be a stern test before the finals weekend in London to round out the international window.
He had offered Craig Casey a chance to impress at scrum-half as first-choice Jamison Gibson-Park returns to full fitness, and he impressed after a slow start.
Ulster back row Nick Timoney also put in a big performance, while Prendergast's showing at fly-half was also largely positive as he put his stamp on the 10 jersey.
When asked if the performances gave him food for thought for selections for the rest of the window, Farrell said: "Definitely, 100%.
"That's exactly what you are after going into next week.
"Having some good competition, we've had it for 10 days in training so how they performed highlights how they have been training.
"Whatever side we pick next week, they'll be competing to play the following week."

articles.headline: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
keyFacts: OpenAI reached a valuation of $1.25 trillion after raising $11 billion in a new funding round reported by Bloomberg.
CEO Sam Altman stated that OpenAI is prioritizing model safety and holding off on an initial public offering for now.
Rival company Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week.
body: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg. That would make it one of the world’s most valuable companies, not long after raising $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion.
OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
CEO Sam Altman said recently that OpenAI is prioritizing safety instead of going ‘guns blazing’ toward an IPO.

Echoing FT and Wall Street Journal reports from last week, Bloomberg says OpenAI is still pursuing additional investments that could increase the amount to $20 billion, and that it had initially hoped to raise as much as $30 billion at a higher valuation of $1.4 trillion. That was before tech stocks dropped, and the results of the midterms showed how much public opinion has turned against AI companies and data center projects.

OpenAI’s rival Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week. Earlier this year, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it’s holding off on its own IPO until it can make more confident claims about its models’ safety. He didn’t give a specific timeline for the IPO, but said at the time, “I think it’s also kind of bad for the world if OpenAI waits too long to go public.”

articles.headline: Democrats blast Trump’s decision to appoint Stephen Miller as chief of staff in wake of Republican midterm rout – live
keyFacts: Donald Trump appointed adviser Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff after Republican midterm election losses.
Democrats and some Republicans condemned the promotion, citing Miller's role as the architect of Trump's hardline deportation agenda.
Miller will start his new role on November 9, while Democrats stated they will investigate him in Congress.
body: Democrats blast Trump’s decision to appoint Stephen Miller as chief of staff in wake of Republican midterm rout – live
Chuck Schumer says the move to promote the controversial immigration hardliner shows that Donald Trump ‘learned nothing from his historic defeat’ in the midterms

Stephen Miller, one of Donald Trump’s fiercest allies and architect of the administration’s hardline deportation agenda, will now be the White House chief of staff. The role is a promotion for Miller, who currently serves as an adviser. Trump said that Miller will start the job on Monday 9 November, less than a week after Republicans’ crushing defeat in the midterm elections.

Wiles will now take a role in Trump’s political operation, which includes his Super Pac Maga Inc. On social media, she said that serving the president has been “the honor of a lifetime”. Wiles has been in the president’s orbit for over a decade, and prior to her role at the White House, she managed, alongside Chris LaCivita, Trump’s winning 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump later told reporters that he decided to promote Miller because he“wanted to make a change”. He praised Wiles, and said that Miller had been by his side “from the beginning”. “Sometimes in life you have to make moves,” the president said.

Meanwhile, Democrats blasted Trump’s decision, after Republicans faced a drubbing in the midterm elections. Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, said that the president “learned nothing from his historic defeat”, and Congressman Robert Garcia – poised to be the chair of the House oversight committee – advised Miller to “lawyer up”. Garcia said that in the majority, Democrats on his panel will “continue to investigate [Stephen] Miller for his misconduct, and we will fight against his hateful policies in Congress and the courts”.

Reading aloud from prepared remarks to NASA officials at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Friday, Donald Trump ran through a list of what he called evidence that Americans were “the greatest pioneers explorers, inventors and innovators who ever lived.”

“America is the nation that dreamed and created the modern world,” Trump said, peering at a teleprompter from beneath a USA cap. “We laid the railroads, harnessed electricity and invented the lightbulb, the telephone, the airplane, the assembly line, the television, the microchip, the personal computer, the internet, GPS, the smartphone, and almost every other thing- think of it – almost every other thing that’s worth mentioning.”

He then looked out at the audience and veered off-script to comment: “That’s a cool list, though, when you think, huh? How about a little piece of each of them? Wouldn’t that be nice? You wouldn’t be sitting here right now. You’d be someplace else.”

The president then returned to his prepared remarks, looking back at the teleprompter and saying: “We charted the human genome to cure diseases,” but stumbled badly over the word “genome” which he pronounced “guh-nome”.

Despite Trump’s attempt to claim that the US deserves credit for sequencing all the DNA in human chromosomes, the Human Genome Project was, in fact, the work of an international network of geneticists.
Trump expresses satisfaction at stock market plunge after Republican losses in midterms, deflects blame from himself

Donald Trump, remarkably, gave yet another speech on Friday, delivering remarks at the John F. Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida in his official capacity as president, which were, nonetheless, threaded through with partisan political talking points.

The president emerged to the theme tune from his rallies, God Bless the USA, and mimed dancing, before starting his speech by celebrating the victories of two Florida Republicans, Byron Donalds, the governor-elect, and senator Ashley Moody.
The pair were the only two candidates Trump rallied for in the past month who won competitive races.

He then praised members of his administration who were present, singling out the US ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, for “the way you took on, the Cubans”. Waltz was recently engaged in a spat with a Cuban official at the UN which played on heavy rotation on Fox News, the president’s window on the world.

Trump then suggested that he was glad that the US stock market plunged after the Republican wipeout at the ballot box, on fears that companies building AI data centers might not be as free to push ahead with regulation by a Democratic Congress.

“Yesterday, you know, our country lost $3 trillion, all because of an election,” Trump said. “If we were to gain $3 trillion, I probably would have been more unhappy. But you know what that means; that means that they thought somebody else did well in an election.”
“By the way, I was not on the ballot, just in case you had any question,” he added. “Because if we were on the ballot, we would’ve won but we weren’t.”
Senator Chris Murphy discharged from hospital after stroke as doctor says he expects full recovery

Senator Chris Murphy was released from a hospital on Friday following treatment for a stroke and plans to spend several weeks at a rehabilitation center as he works to recover, the Connecticut Democrat said in a statement.

“Thank you for the outpouring of support my family and I have received over the last few days,” Murphy said. “I want to be direct with you, so here is my diagnosis. Last Saturday afternoon, I felt something was not right with my body and called 9-1-1 out of an abundance of caution, and I’m glad I did. I was diagnosed with a small bleed in the thalamus region of my brain.”

“The doctors are very encouraged by the progress I’ve made so far. In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today,” he continued.

The senator also released a statement from Dr Jose Suarez, the chief of neurosciences critical care at the Johns Hopkins Hospital. “Senator Murphy experienced a small hemorrhagic stroke. He has shown tremendous progress, and at the current rate of improvement, we expect that he will make a full recovery following rehabilitation,” the doctor said.
Indiana Republican congressman reportedly calls Trump's promotion of Stephen Miller to chief of staff 'a horrible decision'

The morning after the midterm wave that swept away dozens of his colleagues, congressman Marlin Stutzman, an Indiana Republican who held his seat, told voters that Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda was a major factor, and called on the president to fire its architect, Stephen Miller.

“The press ran with it, the Democrats ran with it, and it looked bad on us – the deportation effort,” Stutzman said on Wednesday. “President Obama deported more illegals than what President Trump has. But you know what? he didn’t he didn’t go out and talk about it the way that, you know, we did. I mean, frankly, I think Stephen Miller should be fired this morning. I mean, there needs to be some changs at hte White House.”
Asked by Semafor on Friday what he made of Trump’s decision to not fire but promote Miller, Stutzman told the outlet it was a “horrible decision.”

Several newly elected Democrats and Senator Bernie Sanders have renewed calls for datacenter moratoriums in the days after the US midterm elections. The sweeping Democratic victory, which was buoyed in part by backlash to the tech industry, has added momentum to efforts to slow down the multi-trillion-dollar buildout of the controversial facilities.

On the social media platform X, Sanders posted a call for an immediate national datacenter moratorium this week. “Americans don’t want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment, gutting jobs and threatening humanity’s future,” Sanders said on Wednesday.
Sanders was joined by several Democrats, including Representative Yassamin Ansari of Arizona – a state where Elon Musk’s SpaceX has proposed a datacenter project that would span more than 700 acres.

“Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence,” Ansari posted Wednesday on X. Musk mocked her post in a retweet, and the two sparred, with Ansari forecasting congressional hearings, telling the centi-billionaire: “See you soon.”

The pushback to the buildout of datacenters, which tech companies need to power the AI products that have become central to their businesses, was one of the most visible issues of the midterms. Opposition to datacenters figured heavily in campaigns across the US, while voters passed dozens of local ballot measures aimed at restricting datacenter projects in their states.
Add congressman Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, to the ranks of those deeply alarmed at Donald Trump naming Stephen Miller his new White House chief of staff.
“Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller doubles down on the politics of hatred, lawlessness, and failure that the American people soundly rejected three days ago,” Beyer said in a statement.
He continued:

“Stephen Miller is the architect of Trump’s immigration policies that plunged quiet American communities into violence. At Miller’s direction, peaceful, law-abiding people have been seized from their families and imprisoned or deported for minor civil offenses, and American citizens who protested these actions have been beaten up and even killed by masked paramilitary thugs. Miller is also the ‘brains’ behind the illegal, extrajudicial murders of people in the Caribbean and the Pacific, many of whom may have done nothing wrong. He frequently promised in 2024 that Trump would focus on the economy and avoid new wars, and then became an ardent defender of Trump’s foolish, unpopular attacks on Iran and other countries.

“Stephen Miller embodies the worst elements of the Trump presidency. His promotion shows that Trump has learned nothing from his electoral debacle and has no intention of even trying to work constructively with the next Congress. But Trump and his Republican allies who continue to embrace the politics of hate, division, and chaos are wildly out of step with what the American people want, and they will keep suffering more defeats until they listen.”

Miles Taylor, who served as chief of staff at the Department of Homeland Security during Donald Trump’s first term, and wrote in an anonymous, 2018 New York Times Op-Ed article that he was “working diligently from within” the Trump administration “to frustrate parts of his agenda and his worst inclinations,” has weighed in on the danger of a White House run by Stephen Miller.
Taylor, who later resigned to join the ranks of anti-Trump Republican memoirists and podcasters, warned on Friday:

I spent two years working with Stephen Miller. His appointment as White House chief of staff is among the most dangerous personnel decisions in the history of our republic. I say that without reservation.
Republican congressman Mark Harris has narrowly won reelection to House in North Carolina’s eighth congressional district, defeating Democrat Colby Watson by just over 5,000 votes.

Democrats have won nine House seats in North Carolina so far, to just one for Republicans, with four races still too close to call, including one in which a Democrat leads a Republican incumbent by just 99 votes.
As voters reject Trump's agenda, Stephen Miller says president 'has single-handedly saved America from those who would destroy it'

The elevation of Stephen Miller, the architect of Donald Trump’s brutal and unpopular mass deportation agenda, to White House chief of staff suggests that the president has no intention of rolling back the crackdown, even after voters delivered a sweeping rebuke by electing Democrats to every House seat along the US border with Mexico.
Miller’s appointment has been widely condemned by Democrats, and some Republicans, but the man himself said in a statement that he is “honored beyond words” to run the White House.

“President Trump is the most transformative political leader in American History — and he has single-handedly saved America from those who would destroy it,” Miller said, referring to the incoming Democratic majority in both houses of Congress in typically extreme fashion.

“The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic,” Miller added, in a clear signal that the final two years of Trump’s presidency will pit a maximally combative White House against Congress.
The NAACP’s president, Derrick Johnson, has this to say about the elevation of Stephen Miller, a longtime promoter of white nationalism, to the role of White House chief of staff:
“Stephen Miller belongs nowhere near the Oval Office. He belongs before a judge. He’s a thug who will be remembered as the architect of Trump’s vile and authoritarian regime.”
Hegseth and RFK Jr welcome Miller's promotion to White House chief of staff

Pete Hegseth, the embattled former Fox weekend anchor turned US defense secretary who could face an impeachment vote as soon as next week, was quick to praise new White House chief of staff Stephen Miller on social media, posting a meme of the two men together, with the caption “Stand. Fight. Defend the Republic.” Hegseth tagged both Miller and the White House on X, Elon Musk’s rebranded, rightwing Twitter, to make sure they were aware of his post.

Hegseth, who appears to be leading a coordinated social-media campaign to save his job, used the same caption for a previous post on Thursday, which featured images of himself and one of Donald Trump raising his fist moments after surviving an assassination attempt in 2024.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the health secretary, quickly followed with a post welcoming Miller’s appointment as a supporter of the so-called Make America Health Again movement. “Next to me, Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration,” Kennedy wrote. “It’s time to unleash the Kraken.”

Stephen Miller, one of Donald Trump’s fiercest allies and architect of the administration’s hardline deportation agenda, will now be the White House chief of staff. The role is a promotion for Miller, who currently serves as an adviser. Trump said that Miller will start the job on Monday 9 November, less than a week after Republicans’ crushing defeat in the midterm elections.

Wiles will now take a role in Trump’s political operation, which includes his Super Pac Maga Inc. On social media, she said that serving the president has been “the honor of a lifetime”. Wiles has been in the president’s orbit for over a decade, and prior to her role at the White House, she managed, alongside Chris LaCivita, Trump’s winning 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump later told reporters that he decided to promote Miller because he“wanted to make a change”. He praised Wiles, and said that Miller had been by his side “from the beginning”. “Sometimes in life you have to make moves,” the president said.

Meanwhile, Democrats blasted Trump’s decision, after Republicans faced a drubbing in the midterm elections. Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, said that the president “learned nothing from his historic defeat”, and Congressman Robert Garcia – poised to be the chair of the House oversight committee – advised Miller to “lawyer up”. Garcia said that in the majority, Democrats on his panel will “continue to investigate [Stephen] Miller for his misconduct, and we will fight against his hateful policies in Congress and the courts”.
As Donald Trump traveled to Cape Canaveral, Florida today, he told reporters that he wants Stephen Miller to “run things well” as the new White House chief of staff.
When asked what prompted Miller’s promotion, the president said that he “wanted to make a change”.
“Susie [Wiles] has done a very good job, Stephen’s been great, and we gotta make moves,” Trump said. “Sometimes in life you have to make moves.”
“Stephen’s been with me from the beginning, he gets it, very good politically … a very good manager,” Trump said on his decision to pick Miller for the top job.
Miller is also traveling with Trump to Florida for the president’s remarks at the Kennedy Space Center later today.
Wiles has taken a 'stranglehold on policy decisions' says ex-adviser to health secretary

Against the backdrop of Susie Wiles’ departure from the White House, it’s worth noting that Calley Means, a former senior adviser to health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr who resigned just weeks before the US midterms, said that Wiles is the most “powerful chief of staff in modern American history” who has “taken a stranglehold on policy decisions”.

Means, an architect’s of the administration’s Make America Healthy Again (Maha) agenda, claimed that Wiles’ former work as a lobbyist at Ballard partners had compromised her support for various policies, particularly his proposals to make children’s diets healthier, in order to still receive financial boosts throughout the election cycle.
“Susie said to me many times: ‘We need money for the midterms, Calley. We need money for the midterms,’” Means said on a two-hour episode of Joe Rogan’s podcast.

“It is absolutely true that [Trump’s] administration has been infiltrated by the very people that he energized voters to say he would get out of DC,” Means told Rogan. “Everything in the political strategy was based on getting enough money for the midterms, not actually doing the things that would then energize voters enough.”
Hakeem Jeffries, poised to be next House speaker, calls for Miller to be 'fired'

Congressman Hakeem Jeffries, who is poised to become the next US House speaker when Democrats retake the majority in the new year, called Stephen Miller “a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands”.
Jeffries added: “His [Miller’s] presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor. Fire him today.”

body: Illegal immigrant heard voices to assassinate Trump — arrested with firearm-filled stolen vehicle
By
Bonny Chu, Fox News
Published Nov. 6, 2026, 6:39 p.m. ET
See more of our coverage in your search results.

An illegal immigrant from Venezuela was arrested near the White House on Thursday after he was allegedly found inside a stolen vehicle carrying multiple firearms and reportedly threatening to kill President Donald Trump, according to the Department of Homeland Security.
US Secret Service officers approached the suspect Thursday evening after spotting him “acting suspicious in his car while it was parked on Constitution Avenue in Washington, DC,” DHS told Fox News.
The suspect told officers that he heard voices in his head telling him to come to the nation’s capital and kill Trump, DHS said.
Officers then discovered that the vehicle had been reported stolen, and the suspect admitted to having weapons inside.
During the investigation, officers said they recovered three firearms, including an AR-15-style rifle and two handguns, along with dozens of rounds of ammunition.
The suspect was identified as Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, who illegally entered the country through Texas in March 2024 and was subsequently arrested by US Border Patrol, according to officials.
He was later released into the country under the Biden administration.
Following his arrest, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer for Chrinos with the US Marshals Service, where he is currently in custody.
The US Secret Service said the incident reflects a growing threat posed by armed individuals “drawn to the White House complex.”

“This is the latest example of Secret Service personnel relying on extensive training and experience to deescalate a volatile situation that posed an imminent threat to our protectees and other Americans,” US Secret Service Director Sean Curran said in a statement.

“While our personnel are trained to respond to situations like this and we remain confident in our tactics, we are alarmed by the increase in threat cases that continue to arise,” Curran continued. “The Secret Service will continue expanding our focus on proactively investigating and identifying individuals who make threats to our protectees, in order to disrupt threats before they arrive in Washington.”

articles.headline: Miller time: Trump turns to a die-hard MAGA loyalist ahead of battle with congressional Democrats
keyFacts: President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff following the midterm elections.
Miller succeeds outgoing chief of staff Susie Wiles, who faced growing criticism after Republicans lost control of Congress.
As chief of staff, Miller is expected to manage White House staff and participate in negotiations with incoming Democratic congressional majorities.
body: The day before the midterm election s, incoming White House chief of staff Stephen Miller had a blunt message to voters who were considering staying home or registering their disapproval of President Donald Trump .
“President Trump took a bullet for you, he bled for you, he faced life in prison for you,” Miller told Sean Hannity’s audience on Fox News. “And what he needs from you tomorrow is your vote.”

Like many things that worked well for Republicans in 2024, this pitch didn’t carry the day on Tuesday. But it was typical Stephen Miller: loyal to Trump, apocalyptic in tone, and unflinching in defense of a beleaguered and increasingly divided MAGA movement.
That’s the person Trump will now have running his White House staff .

A former Senate aide to Jeff Sessions who helped the Alabama Republican hone his hard-line immigration stance at a time when many GOP lawmakers were contemplating bipartisan amnesty legislation instead, Miller has been with Trump for most of his decade atop the Republican Party.
Miller has become an unlikely household name, a fixture in Trumpworld, and a relentless pusher of the president’s message inside the White House and on cable news networks.

Now the 41-year-old Miller, who has been serving as deputy chief of staff during Trump’s second term, will take on a new role that typically involves managing the personalities around the president, safeguarding access to the Oval Office, and keeping the Trump train running on time.

Miller would also likely play a key role in negotiations with the incoming Democratic congressional majorities, which is seemingly bad news for anyone who would like to see an immigration deal that involves legalizing large numbers of illegal immigrants — although if anyone’s imprimatur could help sell anything like that to the base, it would be Miller’s.
The promotion may also suggest that the White House intends to fight any Democratic attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth , with whom Miller is close.

Miller will have a tough act to follow in outgoing White House chief of staff Susie Wiles , who became the first woman to hold the job after helping to manage Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign, which culminated in one of the greatest political comebacks in history. She is seen as less dogmatic than Miller and is much shyer in front of the camera, more of a back-of-the-house manager who allowed Miller, Vice President JD Vance , Secretary of State Marco Rubio , former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt , and others to join Trump as the public face of the White House.

Wiles had much greater success managing a mercurial principal than any previous Trump White House chief of staff. Trump ran through four chiefs of staff during his first term, with none lasting longer than 17 months. None had long-standing ties to Trump before taking the job — Reince Priebus had been chairman of the Republican National Committee during the president’s rapid political rise and Mark Meadows had been a key congressional ally — and it is a demanding job where tenures tend to be short.

But there was growing criticism of Wiles in the run-up to what turned out to be a disastrous midterm election in which Republicans lost control of both houses of Congress despite big structural and financial advantages. While some of the buzz undoubtedly came from people disgruntled with their lack of access to Trump under Wiles, the White House has had messaging problems of late.

Eyebrows were raised when two top outside advisers to Trump were reported to be working on foreign political campaigns. There wasn’t much of a coordinated sales pitch for the Iran war, which is now being widely blamed for the GOP’s beating at the ballot box. The short-lived attempt to replace Leavitt as press secretary with Katie Zacharia ended up making Anthony Scaramucci’s stint in government look as long as Anthony Fauci’s.

The midterm election loss was a natural inflection point to make a switch at the chief of staff position regardless of how much responsibility Wiles, a seasoned and successful political operative, ultimately bore. Miller stepping into the breach signals a defiant Trump reacting to electoral defeat by tapping a wartime consigliere rather than an emissary to the establishment.

Congressional Democrats largely view Miller as a zealot, especially fanatical about immigration enforcement. Trump himself once joked that if it was up to Miller, the country’s population would drop to 100 million. Now they will have to talk with him at times.
TRUMP NAMES STEPHEN MILLER WHITE HOUSE CHIEF OF STAFF

A former Trump administration official told the Washington Examiner that in the first term, the president had aides who were loyal, aligned on policy, and good at their jobs. “Stephen was one of the few people who checked all three boxes,” the official said.

Miller’s public reputation is that of a humorless, unsmiling Trump foot soldier, though he is actually well liked by his peers. As Miller boarded Marine One on Friday with Trump, Rubio, and aide Natalie Harp, CNN’s Kaitlan Collins, whose own facial expressions have been the subject of White House scrutiny, reported he was “grinning.”

articles.headline: Here's what's in Path of Exile 2’s huge 1.0 release, coming in December
keyFacts: Path of Exile 2 will release its full 1.0 version on December 11 after two years of early access.
The update adds two new classes, the Shadow and the Duelist, alongside acts five and six to complete the campaign.
The release introduces a new league mechanic called Conquerors of Wraeclast, featuring base building, army recruitment, and castle battles.
body: Path of Exile 2's full release is out on December 11, and coming with it are two new classes, two new acts, a new league, tons of new monsters, bosses, battles, endgame changes, gem updates, atlas and skill tree updates, a new pinnacle boss, base types, uniques, and, I don't know, probably a kitchen sink or something. Let's go over it.

First of all, we'll have two new classes: the Shadow and the Duelist. With them, we'll get all new skill gems for daggers and swords, with tons of new builds available. Daggers introduce new mechanics around stealth, traps, shadow skills with clones that attack with you, and classic skills like blade vortex and fire trap.

The Duelist will introduce swords, and with it fan favorite skills like cyclone and hemorrhage. With swords we'll be able to use stances like blood and sand or ready stance. Add to this being able to two-hand, dual wield, or sword and board and swords look to add a huge amount of mechanical complexity.

After two years of early access, the campaign will finally be fully finished. Acts five and six will complete our story of chasing the Beast through the world, with a return to Oriath and beyond. The campaign will also feature new bespoke rare monsters with their own abilities, appearances, and even mods. In addition, the campaign will feature an introduction to the league mechanic for 1.0, Conquerors of Wraeclast.

The league will feature a base building mechanic, where you recruit armies and build up a castle. As you progress through the campaign, you'll recruit armies to battle against enemy armies. There are over 70 points of interest throughout the campaign that let you recruit new types of soldiers for your army, and battle through to kill the boss and get loot.

As you progress your base, you can recruit commanders that will be able to take your recruits and fight battles for you. Like Kingsmarch in Path of Exile 1, these commanders can run maps for you, letting you convert your gold into progress through the atlas and lots of loot. Your castle gets upgraded just like Heroes of Might and Magic, with a beautiful base that you can spend gold to upgrade.

After all the pinnacle bosses and campaign, you can use your armies to battle against other players. Depending on which of the three factions you choose to join (Karui, Ezomyte, or Marraketh), you can battle to take control of various castles around the atlas. As long as your faction controls a castle, you can travel to it on the Atlas to skip around and get to sweet new maps, and you'll receive additional item rarity. It also unlocks hunting grounds nearby that feature rare monsters with increased loot. You'll be able to use currency you find in battle to craft gear, a system which lets you pick mods to remove and reroll into new fractured mods.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
All of the new campaign areas feature new bosses, which you'll also face in the endgame in over 25 new maps.

The endgame has been updated as well—in addition to being able to use castles to jump around the atlas, the atlas skill tree has been substantially changed. Instead of 300+ nodes, it's been trimmed way down to about 70. If you beeline the skills, you should end up with about 50 of 70 by the time you battle against the Arbiter of Divinity.

Tons of gems have been updated. Not only are we getting new gems for daggers and swords, but they've added new skills for existing weapons as well. Support gems have been overhauled so that they're more useful as well, like all of the different elemental penetration gems being rolled into one called elemental penetration. Support gems like brutality are also better, with less of a penalty for chaos damage. Chain support becomes just an upgrade, without the penalty to damage on the initial hit.

The passive tree has had huge changes. In addition to a bunch of new nodes, they've changed how jewels work. Instead of always being located on the travel nodes on the outside of the tree, they'll be located in actual skill clusters. Hopefully this will prevent all of our endgame skill trees looking the same, with a big circle maximizing jewel slots and nothing else.

With tons of new items including base types and uniques, there will be lots of new loot to find. Some of the base types look insanely powerful, like an armor that makes you immune to curses. They've overhauled over 70 uniques and added about 40 more, which should make finding uniques way more exciting, especially in the campaign.

Taken all together, 1.0 looks like it will be an incredible moment for Path of Exile 2, both for players who've been waiting to play it, and for those of us who already have hundreds or thousands of hours in the ARPG. The full release of Path of Exile 2 will be available on December 11.

Russ has been playing PC games since the top of the line graphics were in ASCII and has been obsessed with them just about as long. After a coordinated influence campaign to bamboozle his parents into getting a high speed internet connection to play EverQuest, his fate was well and truly sealed. When he's not writing about videogames, he's teaching karate, cooking an overly complicated dish, or attempting to raise his daughter with a well rounded classical education (Civilization, Doom, and Baldur's Gate, of course). He's probably mapping in Path of Exile right now.

articles.headline: How to get the Piercing Gaze Hunter Mask in The Division 2: Echoes of Central Park
keyFacts: Players must access the Echoes of Central Park DLC in The Division 2 to obtain the Piercing Gaze Hunter mask.

body: The Piercing Gaze Hunter mask is a secret item you can unearth in The Division 2 , but you’ll need to gain access to the Echoes of Central Park DLC. Then, you’ll have to solve a set of clues and recover few letters to get your hands on this mask.
Let’s find out how to get this secret gear added to your in-game collection.
How to obtain the Piercing Gaze Hunter Mask in The Division 2

Screenshot by Destructoid First, you have to head to the location shown on the image below. Go to Lincoln Square district, and the spot will have a wall covered in leaves. It’s not difficult to find, and you’ll notice a bunch of text saying “Break my Walls”.

Screenshot by Destructoid Shoot the wall, and you’ll find letters on it. Keep shooting until all the letters are visible. This is the first location where you find the letters. However, there’s a second location where you’ll find more of these letters.

Screenshot by Destructoid Head to the marked spot on the image above, and you’ll find a second wall with the text “Break my Walls” written on it. Again, start shooting until you get three different letters.

Screenshot by Destructoid Once the parts mentioned above have been solved, go to the southern part of the Lincoln Square District. You’ll find a roof with plant pots and statue, and you need to destroy all of them.
Some of these pots will be indestructible, and you need to keep shooting at them. This will eventually summon the Hunter.

Screenshot by Destructoid To get your mask, you’ll have to defeat the Hunter as it’s the only way. As long as you stay clear from the Seeker Mines, you shouldn’t have any problem defeating the Hunter and obtaining the secret mask.

body: WTA chair apologises to Jessica Pegula after airing of 'diva' comment about Mirra Andreeva, confirms audio deactivated on practice courts at Indian Wells

articles.headline: Paraguay Senate dismisses President Santiago Pena over bank crisis
keyFacts: Paraguay's Senate impeached and convicted former President Santiago Pena over a banking crisis, stripping him of immunity and lifetime Senate status.
Vice President Pedro Alliana will succeed Pena to serve the remainder of the presidential term until August 2028.
Prosecutors ordered the arrest of Pena and former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo following the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank.
body: Paraguay's Senate on Friday impeached President Santiago Pena over a banking crisis that left millions of people unable to access their deposits.
Senators voted overwhelmingly to remove Pena for misconduct in office.
The move cleared the way for Vice President Pedro Alliana to succeed him. He will serve the rest of the presidential term, which ends in August 2028.

Pena had already resigned on Thursday, but by impeaching and convicting him instead of accepting his resignation, senators stripped him of the lifetime Senate seat and immunity granted to former presidents, leaving him vulnerable to prosecution.
Following the Senate vote, prosecutors ordered the arrest of the ousted president alongside former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation.
Officials later said Pena was placed under house arrest pending a decision by the public prosecutor's office on the final charges against him.
Dozens of protesters gathered outside his residence in the capital Asuncion, while police maintained a security cordon around the property.
Why did Pena face impeachment?
Pena's rapid downfall came amid mounting pressure over the collapse of digital lender Ueno, one of the country's biggest banks, with which he had ties.
The bank's accounts — also used to process pension payments — are frozen, leaving millions of customers unable to access their money. Ueno also held hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds.
Pena's resignation on Thursday followed the withdrawal of support by Congress President Basilio Nunez and ruling conservative Colorado Party leader Horacio Cartes.

Thirty-five opposition lawmakers and ruling-party dissidents had submitted impeachment articles in the 80-seat Chamber of Deputies, accusing Pena of conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and institutional cover-ups linked to Ueno.
Pena sold his shares in Ueno Holding, whose businesses include the bank, in April 2025. Lawmakers also cited two loans he received from Ueno as part of allegations of improper financial gain.

They alleged improper presidential interference in the Social Security Institute, known as IPS, and preferential treatment for Ueno. IPS manages pension and health care funds for most Paraguayan workers and held $355 million at the bank — about 9% of its investments, according to financial manager Gladys Vera.

The motion also questioned Pena's 2023 appointment of central bank chief Carvallo, who previously chaired Financiera Ueno. According to the document, the central bank approved the company's conversion into a bank just 83 days after his appointment.
What happened to Ueno Bank?
Ueno served about 2.94 million customers, roughly 60% of Paraguay's adult population.

As of last month, the bank said it held roughly $800 million in public-sector deposits — about a quarter of its total deposits — including money from the operators of Paraguay's giant hydroelectric dams.
Paraguay's central bank ordered a resolution or closure process Tuesday after finding that Ueno's solvency ratio had fallen below half the required minimum.
Ueno's app, card payments and transfers stopped working, while branches closed, leaving customers queuing outside unable to withdraw their savings.
Hundreds of employees of Ueno and other companies in its parent conglomerate protested outside the Labor Ministry Thursday, demanding unpaid wages and severance.
Retirees, depositors, students and workers had marched through Asuncion a day earlier, demanding Pena's impeachment and holding signs saying "Give us back our money."
What have authorities done?

Authorities detained eight senior executives, including founder Miguel Vazquez and bank president Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud.
Lawyers for several detainees said they needed time to review the allegations before commenting.
Pena had sought to reassure customers in a video message Wednesday, pledging legislation "that will return to every saver what they are entitled to as quickly as possible."
The crisis also forced him to cancel his attendance at the Ibero-American summit in Madrid.
Pena, a conservative economist, took office in August 2023 for a five-year term.
Editor's Note: This piece, originally published on November 5, was updated on November 7 to reflect the latest developments.

articles.headline: Trump doubles down on everything that lost him the midterms
keyFacts: President Donald Trump announced that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.
Susie Wiles resigned after Trump was reportedly angry with her over Republican losses in the midterm elections.
Stephen Miller will officially begin his new role as White House chief of staff on Monday, according to Trump.
body: Donald Trump speaks to reporters on Air Force One as Stephen Miller and Karoline Leavitt watch on July 29, 2025. | Andrew Harnik/Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: President Donald Trump is doubling down after a midterm annihilation.

What happened? On Friday afternoon, Trump announced that longtime aide Stephen Miller would take over as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. In a post to Truth Social, Trump said that Miller would start on Monday, but the change appears to be effective more or less immediately — Wiles has already resigned .

Why the change? Trump was reportedly angry with Wiles over the GOP’s collapse in the midterm elections, which saw Democrats winning up and down the ballot even in traditionally deep-red parts of the country.
Trump, for his part, told reporters on Friday that Wiles had “done a very good job.” But, he added, “we gotta make moves. Sometimes in life, you have to make moves.”

What should I know about Miller? Miller is currently the White House deputy chief of staff for policy, as well as homeland security adviser. More importantly, he’s the architect and engine of some of Trump’s most vicious immigration policies, including family separation (during the first Trump term) and ICE’s current campaign of indiscriminate, militarized immigration enforcement.
He’s also an ally of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who has to be feeling a little bit better about his imperiled job (though it won’t keep Hegseth from facing impeachment in the near future).

What does this mean for the Trump presidency? More of the same, cranked up to 11. Miller is as hardline as they come, and he’s certain to push Trump to be even more aggressive on immigration and attempts to use the machinery of government to attack their shared political enemies .

It’s all going to be extraordinarily unpopular, if Tuesday’s midterm results are anything to go by — but with just over two years left in the White House, there’s little reason to believe that Miller and Trump won’t try to push the power of the presidency to its breaking point.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

Let’s end the week on a high note with this piece from my colleague Christian Paz, who writes that “the decency was the point” for voters and Democratic candidates alike in the 2026 midterms. You can read it here with a gift link.
If you’d prefer something even lighter to head into the weekend, I also recommend the Smithsonian’s cheetah cam . Enjoy, have a great weekend, and we’ll see you on Monday!

articles.headline: Apple Says There Are Now 100,000 Apps Built for the iPhone Duo
keyFacts: Apple announced that over 100,000 apps are now built for the iPhone Duo to use the 4:3 main screen.
Susan Prescott stated that thousands of optimized apps and developer workshops are being added to the App Store.
Apple will add a Made for iPhone Duo badge to product pages to help users identify compatible apps.
body: Apple’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, may have come last to the foldable party, as CNET’s review noted, but it’s certainly not least. Senior reporter Abrar Al-Heeti praised it for the iOS 27 integration across both displays and its impressive durability, which has crossed 300,000 folds in our test and counting.

However, as the Duo has filtered down to the general public, some new owners have noted that some of their favorite apps aren’t well optimized for the larger 4:3 inner display. I noticed this myself when I opened the iPhone Duo and launched Discord, finding the app centered on the screen with black space on both sides, rather than expanding to fill the panel.

That’s not unusual for a phone with a brand-new hardware design, and we’ve seen it on many Android foldables, with optimized apps taking a little bit of time to roll out. Apple has confirmed that this is already changing, with over 100,000 apps built for the iPhone Duo to more fully take advantage of the 4:3 main screen.
More from CNET

“Today, there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations in a comment sent to CNET.

“In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users,” Prescott said. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.”

Among the apps, Microsoft Word and Outlook have been adjusted to look similar to their desktop versions, while Zoom uses the inner display as a bigger video conference room. Additionally, the company has confirmed that sports fans can use the NBA and NHL apps to follow live games and highlights on the larger screen.

Etsy and LTK Creator will also show more products in the feed, and productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra will make more use of the additional screen real estate. There’s also Halide Mark III, a pro camera app that adapts to every pose, from a viewfinder on the cover screen when closed to a waist-level viewfinder with one tap when half open.
The iOS 27.2 update should also add support for Apple Pencil (USB-C), letting Duo users in various compatible apps, like Apple Notes, work directly on documents.
Apple shared a list of apps that have been recently optimized for the iPhone Duo, breaking them down into categories like Work, AI, Finances, News and more.
- Watch and Listen: Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (UK), Apple Music Classical
- Sports: NBA, NHL, Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada)
- Stay Connected: Facebook Messenger, Google Chat
- AI: ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot
- Work: Zoom, Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SAP Concur, monday.com
- Productivity: Extra, Goodnotes, PDF Expert, Documents, iA Writer
- News: Substack, The Washington Post, Yahoo News, Fox News
- Finances: Kalshi, Yahoo Finance
- Capture and Create: Halide Mark III, Canva, Suno
- Lifestyle: Etsy, LTK Creator, Tinder, Google Translate
- Health and Fitness: Strava, Alma, Withings, MyFitnessPal, Bevel
- Travel: Transit, Citi Bike, ParkMobile, Viator, Tesla Robotaxi, Priceline
- Food and Dining: Kroger, Domino’s, Taco Bell, Untappd
- Weather and Sky: The Weather Channel, Fox Weather, RainViewer

This isn’t an exclusive list by any means. CNET previously confirmed seven iPhone Duo-ready apps that make the most of Apple’s foldable screen: Netflix, NYT Cooking, Fantastical, Edits by Instagram, TikTok, Instagram and Toastie.

Apple fans have put together their own “does it work on iPhone Duo?” web tracker, giving you a sense of whether an app is fully optimized, partially fits or is still awaiting updates. I can confirm that Discord is currently listed as “partially fits,” meaning it uses most of the inner screen but not all of it, which tracks with my own experience with the letterboxing.

We expect that this is only the beginning, and we’ll see the list above expand in the coming weeks as updated apps are submitted to the App Store. Going forward, you should also see spotlights for iPhone Duo apps in categories like “Great Apps and Games” and “Popular Apps.” Apple is making it easier to identify apps compatible with the iPhone Duo by adding a Made for iPhone Duo badge to product pages.

articles.headline: EA HQ Graced With 'Save Mass Effect' Truck as N7 Day Looms
keyFacts: Fans belonging to the group We are Mass Effect parked a truck displaying a Save Mass Effect message outside EA headquarters.
The campaign aims to raise awareness about the human impact of EA shutting down BioWare and putting the franchise on hold.
Organizers stated that another billboard will appear near BioWare's former offices and a final billboard will launch during The Game Awards next month.
body: Mass Effect fans have taken their mission to save BioWare and its beloved sci-fi franchise to EA headquarters with a truck displaying the #SaveMassEffect message.

The latest update to what has ballooned into a full-blown movement arrived today when the dedicated group of fans known as We are Mass Effect announced they had brought their latest billboard right to the publisher's front door. Where their last push arrived in the form of a daylong billboard in New York City's Times Square , this mobile effort will see a truck sharing the word on the streets surrounding EA and EA Sports HQ in Redwood City, California.

Anyone who visits the area today can spot the truck, which features signage updated with a handy QR code and website URL directing curious players to SaveMassEffect.com . The goal, as We are Mass Effect's Mer told IGN, is to "spread the word and bring as much attention to the movement as possible, " but putting it in EA's front lawn after the publisher put Mass Effect games on hold and shuttered BioWare also sends a message of its own.
🚨 WE ARE BACK ON THE STREETS
Together with @kalaelizabeth, our first mobile billboard is now outside EA's HQ and EA Sports HQ.
📸 If you're nearby, send us pictures! Please don't enter EA's property.
#SaveMassEffect https://t.co/5N87nz8uDR
— We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) November 6, 2026

"Social media can sometimes make devastating events feel distant or abstract," We are Mass Effect told IGN when asked about the truck. "It’s easy to read about these news online without fully grasping the human impact behind it. So we wanted to bring the movement into the physical world and make that support visible. We want to remind people that real people have been impacted by the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the game. We wanted to show them that there is a community that deeply cares about the legacy they’ve created. For us this has never been just about the IP but the people behind it and their work."

Driving a truck around EA HQ will certainly gather some attention, but detractors have warned that no amount of momentum will get the publisher to budge. The goal, as We are Mass Effect has outlined, is not only to offer a message of unity for those who love BioWare franchises like Mass Effect or Dragon Age, but to raise awareness about the human beings affected by these changes, too.

Another mobile billboard will appear near BioWare's former offices tomorrow, with the final billboard launching during The Game Awards next month. Billboard organizer, fundraiser, and content creator Kala Elizabeth told IGN the plan is to drive it around the TGA ceremony for around four hours.

"For me, after our billboards are up, I plan to support the devs however possible and bring visibility to anything else that we can support, but as of right now, I don't have any plans to crowdfund more billboards because these were already exhausting," Elizabeth added with a laugh.
Our first #SaveMassEffect mobile billboard is outside of EA HQ and EA Sports HQ in Redwood! Go get a picture! (do not go into EA if you do) https://t.co/1L3vTqTojP
— Kala Elizabeth #SaveMassEffect (@kalaelizabeth) November 6, 2026

Meanwhile, We are Mass Effect said it is currently putting the finishing touches on a video featuring Mass Effect fans, actors, and contributors for N7 Day tomorrow, November 7. Included in the lineup are Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer. The group is also pushing N7 Play Day in an attempt to boost Steam player numbers for Mass Effect: Legendary Edition .

"And, as a fun throwback to 2012, we’re planning to send cupcakes decorated in N7 colors to EA’s headquarters in Redwood City next week," the group said. "There’s a lot happening, and we don’t plan on stopping anytime soon. The response from the community has shown us just how much Mass Effect and BioWare’s legacy mean to people, and we want to continue finding creative ways to make that support visible."

EA closed down BioWare weeks ago, but as fans get ready for N7 Day, they've done anything but go gently into the night. In addition to that Times Square billboard, a petition urging EA to allow the franchise to live in some capacity has gained more than 300,000 signatures . Save Mass Effect graffiti was also reportedly spray-painted outside of an EA office building in Madrid , while another was decorated with tombstones featuring shuttered studios .

"People are upset, not only about what happened to BioWare, but about the many studios, IPs, and talented devs that have gone through the same thing," We are Mass Effect added. "What we can do is to encourage them to keep supporting the initiatives that the community are organizing, and to keep showing up. We don't want this to become another story, another beloved IP that is forgotten. The most important thing is to make sure people continue paying attention and understand just how much these games and the devs behind them mean to so many."

"I think the most important thing is supporting the devs and showing that we care," Elizabeth said. "N7 Day is a huge day for Mass Effect and this year is very different. It's important that we're loud and show our support. Signing the petition, using the hashtag, and amplifying the voices of the devs."

A new documentary that filmed the studio's final years was announced just yesterday. While fans hope to make a difference at EA's front door, the publisher is still pushing merchandise for the paused franchise for N7 Day . Meanwhile, a Canadian politician has recently joined the fight .

articles.headline: Three Free Games You Can Play For Free This Weekend On PC
keyFacts: Payday 3 and Age of Wonders 4 are temporarily free to play on Steam until November 9.
Flotsam is free to claim and keep on the Epic Games Store until November 12.
Humble Bundle subscribers in November receive PC game keys including Mafia: The Old Country and The Outer Worlds 2.
body: It’s Friday! Welcome to the weekend. We made it. Halloween. Election day. The launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. We survived. I’m about to go pick up Chinese takeout for my family, but before I do, here are some good deals on PC games to kick things off in November.

First, we have games that are temporarily free on Steam. Payday 3, which remains in recovery mode after its terrible launch, is yours to try risk-free until November 9. You can go download it, grab some friends, and try to pull off a few heists without spending a dime. “Launched badly, but it’s slowly taking a turn for the better,” one Steam reviewer recently posted. “To me personally, I love it now, but I can also see that it needs some more spice to give it enough kick for everyone. Will keep supporting and keep genuinely hoping that it could pull a Cyberpunk 2077 moment.”

Second, we have Age of Wonders 4, a generally quite good 4X strategy RPG. It’s also available to play for free until November 9. If you want a fantasy game that mixes empire building with fun tactical battles, Age of Wonders 4strikes a pretty good balance. Players are still encountering bugs and multiplayer issues, but if you just want to settle in for some cozy city building and battles and have a PC with an Nvidia GeForce GTX 670 card or better, it’s a good deal.

Moving over to the Epic Games Store, floating city management sim Flotsam is free to claim until November 12. It’s a feel-good post-apocalyptic game about salvaging debris, meeting fellow survivors, and combing through skill trees to help rebuild civilization. It’s vibrant, chill, and normally $25. And unlike Age of Wonders 4 and Payday 3, it’ll be yours to keep. If you haven’t already played it, this one’s worth having in your library.

Finally, a bonus round. I don’t usually recommend Humble Bundle’s monthly subscription, but the games for November are wroth a look. If you’re willing to sign-up, members this month are getting PC keys for Mafia: The Old Country, The Outer Worlds 2, Shinobi: Art of Vengeance, and a bunch more games. Those three alone are well worth it, but horror shooter Crisol: Theater of Idols, which only released back in February, is also part of the mix. You can read our review of it here.

articles.headline: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
keyFacts: OpenAI raised $11 billion in an ongoing funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reported.
The funding round could total about $20 billion and is expected to close in the coming weeks, a source told Bloomberg.
OpenAI previously delayed plans to go public this year and is now expected to hold an initial public offering next year.
body: OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion.

Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg.
In late September, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion in the upcoming round. The current figures fall well short of that target.
TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment and will update this story if it responds.

The news comes only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the IPO of OpenAI’s chief competitor, Anthropic, are eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted. Bloomberg writes that some potential buyers believe Anthropic’s valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion that investors were said to be expecting roughly a month ago.
OpenAI previously intimated that it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans. There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point.

The market for AI hangs in a particularly precarious place. The Democratic landslide in the U.S. midterms — and overwhelmingly negative voter sentiment around data centers — has caused jitters throughout the market, with many anticipating potential regulatory challenges in the future.

articles.headline: All Happy Mask Shop buyer locations in Zelda Ocarina of Time
keyFacts: Polygon reports the Happy Mask Shop quest in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time requires Young Link to sell various masks to specific customers across Hyrule.
Polygon states players must pay the salesman a set going cost after selling each mask, often using their own rupees when customers pay less than required.
Polygon explains completing the mask sales unlocks additional masks, including the Mask of Truth which allows players to hear the thoughts of NPCs and animals.
body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's Happy Mask Shop quest sends you around Hyrule peddling masks to specific customers. That sounds like a cushy gig, except you have very little guidance about who your customers are, and you occasionally even have to pay back the cost of the mask, too. However, if you want a big chunk of cash and a chance to see and hear everything in Ocarina of Time, it's worth the hassle.
Below, we walk you through each step of the Ocarina of Time remake's Happy Mask Shop quest and explain what you get for your trouble.
How to start the Happy Mask Shop quest in Ocarina of Time

Visit the Happy Mask Shop in Hyrule Castle Town as Young Link at any point during the adventure after you've met Princess Zelda and given her letter to the Death Mountain gatekeeper. The shop is in Castle Town square, and it's only open during the daytime.

Speak with the salesman to get started. He'll offer you a gig selling masks, and the first one is the Keaton Mask. He tells you the going cost is 10 rupees, which means that's how much you have to pay him after selling the mask, and then sends you off. This pattern repeats for the rest of the quest. After delivering a mask, you must pay the salesman the going cost to get the next one. Your customers won't always pay the going cost, either, so you'll frequently have to foot the bill yourself.
Keaton Mask buyer location in Ocarina of Time

Depending on how many people you talk to, you might have an idea about this one already. After you chat with the Death Mountain gatekeeper about the Hylian Shield, he'll mention a trendy mask that his child wants and not-so-subtly ask you to get it for him if you can. That's the Keaton Mask. Return to the gatekeeper, equip the mask from the equipment menu, and speak to him. He'll offer to buy the mask for 15 rupees.
Hand it over, return to the salesman, and pay the 10-rupee fee. Next, you get the Skull Mask, which has a going rate of 20 rupees.
Skull Mask buyer location in Ocarina of Time

The Skull Mask is for the Skull Kid, a child who hangs out in the Lost Woods and resembles a Deku Scrub. Enter the Lost Woods from Kokiri Forest, and immediately turn left. You'll walk into the Skull Kid's clearing. Equip the Skull Mask, stand on the small stump, target him with ZL, and he'll demand the mask. He gives you 10 rupees for it, so you'll have to scrape together the other 10 for the salesman's fee yourself.
Head back to the Happy Mask Shop, fork over the fee, and choose the Spooky Mask next. This one has a going rate of 30 rupees.
Spooky Mask buyer location in Ocarina of Time

"Are spooky things popular?" Navi asks after you get the mask, and the answer is yes, but only for one person whom you haven't even had a reason to meet yet. It's the kid who hangs out in Kakariko Village's graveyard during the day. He wanders around the graveyard, but if you're there shortly after sunrise, you can catch him right at the entrance.

Anyway, the little guy is a big fan of Dampe the gravekeeper, and since he wants to be just like him, he's willing to buy your Spooky Mask. The kid pays a hefty 50-rupee price, so you don't have to give the salesman your own money this time. You even get 20 rupees for yourself!
Head back to the shop, and get the Bunny Hood. It's an expensive mask (well, hood) and costs 50 rupees.
Bunny Hood buyer location in Ocarina of Time

Selling the Bunny Hood is a little more complex. The postman is your customer, but he won't start appearing until after you obtain all three Spiritual Stones, which means completing Dodogno's Cavern and Jabu-Jabu's Belly. After that, he'll run quickly around Hyrule Field in a broad oval that loops around Lon-Lon Ranch. Equip the hood, catch up to him, and he'll offer a gold rupee for it. That's 200 rupees, so you're making a 150-rupee profit off this sale.
Return to the Happy Mask Shop to pay the fee. This time, you'll have several masks to choose from, though no customers. You can get:
- Goron Mask
- Zora Mask
- Gerudo Mask
- Mask of Truth

Wearing any of the first three will lead to a few unique dialogue lines when you speak to people while wearing them, but they aren't tied to any secrets or quests. The Mask of Truth is the real catch, though. Wearing it lets you get messages from Gossip Stones, listen in to NPC thoughts, and hear the thoughts of animals, like that cow in a hole on Death Mountain. You don't need the mask to get milk from the cow, but at least it gives the poor beast someone to talk to. Some of the things that NPCs are thinking are pretty interesting, too.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a little bit different than the original game, so if you need guides to help you through, we don’t blame you. We have walkthroughs for all the dungeons, from the Deku Tree to Ganondorf's Castle. We also have guides for the sillier, in-between parts of the game, like when you have to find Richard (the dog) or Cuccos.
For those going for 100% completion, we also have guides on where to find every Piece of Heart, every Gold Skulltula token, and where to plant every Magic Bean.

articles.headline: What Trump’s pick of Stephen Miller for chief of staff means for rest of his presidency
keyFacts: President Trump appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff following Republican defeats in the midterm elections.
Supporters said Miller will help advance the America First agenda, while administration officials praised his loyalty and organizational skills.
Democrats and some Republicans criticized the appointment, citing concerns over Miller and his hardline immigration policies.
body: WASHINGTON — It’s Miller time — and the gloves are off!

President Trump pulled out his bulldog Stephen Miller as he prepares for an epic fight with Democrats following Tuesday’s blue tsunami — announcing Miller as his new chief of staff in anticipation of a showdown with Capitol Hill.
“The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic,” Miller said Friday.
The elevation of Miller was widely viewed as Trump doubling down on his America First agenda and arming up for battles ahead with Democrats promising sprawling inquiries.
“I don’t think there could be any choice that sends a better message to our fractured base than Miller,” said a source close to the White House.
“He understands our coalition and is the choice best equipped to help rebuild it as we spend the next two years in a constant war with the Democrat-controlled Congress.”
Miller replaces Susie Wiles, who stepped down Friday, taking the fall for Republicans’ brutal defeat in Tuesday’s midterm elections.
He served as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser since Trump’s return to the White House and was a senior adviser and top speechwriter in his first term.

“Many people know Stephen for his fierce loyalty to the president, but more than that, he is the administration’s most organized and competent operator,” said Taylor Budowich, a former deputy chief of staff for communications and personnel who worked alongside Miller in the West Wing.
“He has built and managed one of the most effective policy teams in American history. He was born to be Donald Trump’s chief of staff.”

Miller received an outpouring of support from high-profile administration officials, with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. writing: “Next to me, Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration. It’s time to unleash the Kraken.”
Attorney General Todd Blanche wrote that he was “looking forward to continuing our work with my good friend Stephen Miller as Chief.”

“Together we’ve reduced crime to historic levels, enhanced public safety throughout our communities, and continue to root out the massive fraud that has taken advantage of American taxpayers,” Blanche wrote. “We’re not slowing down.”
But Miller, whose strident personality is a sharp break from Wiles’ more modest demeanor, drew immediate condemnation from Democrats and qualms from some fellow Republicans.
“Stephen Miller is a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands,” tweeted top House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY).
“His presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor. Fire him today.”

Miller has had a broad portfolio during Trump’s second term, but he’s best-known for pushing for accelerated deportations of illegal immigrants, which the president vowed to do during his 2024 comeback campaign.

Although polls showed most Hispanic voters supported mass deportations in the abstract in 2024 and voted for Trump in droves, the community recoiled at anecdotal cases, with Republicans shedding Hispanic support in the midterms, dashing GOP hopes for a lasting realignment.
“Miller as COS? Full Gestapo it is,” said a prominent Republican consultant, describing Miller, who is Jewish, as a “good guy” who would nonetheless bring an “iron fist” to management and policy.
“Hispanic voters were already heading for the exits,” this person added. “Nice of us to hold the door.”

Rep. Marlin Stutzman (R-Ind.), who will serve in the much-reduced Republican caucus next year, called for Miller to be fired after the election and told Semafor his elevation was a “horrible decision.”
Retiring anti-Trump Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) told CNN, “it is a colossal mistake and the last thing we need 72 hours after the ass whooping we got on Tuesday.”
Some Republican blowback was hardly a surprise.
Asked in September what Republicans could do to regain Hispanic support, Latinas for Trump founder Ileana Garcia, a Florida state senator, told The Post: “Fire Stephen Miller!”

Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.), who leads in vote tabulations for re-election, filmed a campaign video in front of the White House denouncing the deportations, urging Trump to “be careful what your advisers are telling you about immigration policy; The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed.”
